workers.definition: people who do particular jobs, especially ones involving physical or practical effort.
workers.example: The workers moved the artefact with great caution.

workforce.definition: all the people who work for a particular company, industry or country.
workforce.example: The integration of new immigrants into the workforce strengthened the whole town's economy.

working.definition: doing a job, or in a state of operating correctly.
working.example: Rough planks and old rope soon became a working loom.

workplace.definition: the place where someone does their job.
workplace.example: "That is a sharp observation," the teacher praised, "about how teamwork improves any workplace."

works.definition: operates correctly, or does a job.
works.example: Look how carefully she works at that loom, Nora!

workshop.definition: a room or building where things are made or repaired using tools, or a session where people learn a skill together.
workshop.example: Dina sat quietly among the wreckage of her workshop.

workshops.definition: rooms or buildings where things are made or repaired, or sessions where people learn a skill together.
workshops.example: The local capitalist reinvested her profits and opened two more workshops in the growing town.

world.definition: the Earth and all the people, places and things on it.
world.example: Samira, imagine a world where phones never existed!

world's.definition: belonging to, or relating to, the world.
world's.example: Long ago, the villagers believed the world's sky had broken.

worlds.definition: planets or other large bodies in space, or separate spheres of existence.
worlds.example: "A supernova scatters the very atoms that later build new worlds," the teacher said.

worried.definition: feeling anxious or troubled about something.
worried.example: Worried families found it hard to sleep that week.

worry.definition: to feel anxious or uneasy about something that might happen.
worry.example: Don't worry, Adam, I've already sorted the tickets for tonight!

worsens.example: Rapid deforestation destroys the homes of countless animals and worsens flooding across the region.

writer.definition: a person who writes books, articles or other pieces of text, especially as an occupation.
writer.example: The writer used a relative clause to describe the cheetah's speed.

writer's.definition: belonging to, or relating to, a person who writes.
writer's.example: A single sentence can sometimes reveal a writer's true opinion.

writers.definition: people who write books, articles or other texts, especially as an occupation.
writers.example: Why do science writers so often use the present tense?

writing.definition: the activity of putting words down on paper or another surface, or a piece of written text.
writing.example: Have you ever tried writing your own poetry?

written.definition: expressed or recorded using words put down on paper or another surface.
written.example: Wasn't that story written a very long time ago?

wrong.definition: not correct, or not morally right.
wrong.example: Sami, you folded the chart the wrong way, it will not open properly!

wrote.definition: put words down on paper or another surface.
wrote.example: Adam wrote a catchy slogan for the class fundraiser.

yard.definition: an outdoor area, often next to a building, used for a particular purpose such as storage or work.
yard.example: Why are the hens scattering seed all over the yard?

year.example: May I join the basketball team this year?

yearly.example: The accountant checked the figures twice before presenting the company's yearly report.

years.example: Was the Scholar imprisoned for many years?

yoghurt.definition: a thick, slightly sour food made from milk that has had bacteria added to it.
yoghurt.example: Do you prefer the smooth texture of yoghurt or the crunch of fresh, roasted nuts?

you'll.definition: a short form of 'you will', used to say what will happen to or be done by the person being spoken to.
you'll.example: 'Watch out or you'll collide!' Sami shouted as the cyclists raced towards each other.

young.definition: in an early stage of life or development; not old.
young.example: What a polite young man Omar has become!

younger.definition: less old than someone or something else, or less old than before.

youngest.definition: least old among a group of people.
youngest.example: "Even a meagre saving matters," Omar reminded the youngest shoppers.

yourself.definition: used to refer back to the person being spoken to, when they are also the subject of the sentence.
yourself.example: Well done, young boy, you found the path yourself!

youth.definition: young people considered as a group, or the period of a person's life when they are young.
youth.example: New ideas and old tradition met together at the youth assembly.
